title: How to Write Usefully
candidate_workflows: Before publishing important founder or product communication, test each claim for correctness, importance, novelty, and strength; narrow, qualify, or delete claims that cannot remain both precise and true.
Draft quickly enough to explore branches, then revise repeatedly until doubtful or clumsy passages are resolved; use the full range of qualifications to communicate actual certainty and scope.
Write in the simplest language that preserves the idea, both to reduce reader effort and to expose mistakes that ornate prose can hide.

When a disagreement may be based on misrepresentation, ask for the exact passage and the reason it is false; preempt reasonable misunderstandings in the text without optimizing for deliberate bad-faith readings.
Start with a narrow topic where you have real expertise and use private drafts to discover the idea before expanding the audience or deciding to publish.

title: Coronavirus and Credibility
exclusion_reason: A topical reflection on pundits' false COVID predictions and credibility; it supplies no founder, team, product, user, or work decision process beyond the generic admonition to remember failed forecasts.

title: Orthodox Privilege
exclusion_reason: A social and political argument about conventional-minded people's blindness to unsayable truths; it contains no startup or maker decision, team practice, user insight, or operational workflow.

title: The Four Quadrants of Conformism
candidate_workflows: When evaluating a founder for a venture that depends on a nonconsensus insight, assess independent judgment separately from social polish: look for the ability to question rules and remain right when peers disagree.
Distinguish genuine independence from performative rebellion by identifying whose rules a person follows; flouting authority in the same way as one's peers is still conformity.
Protect idea-generating teams with norms that permit discussion of apparently bad ideas and leave a margin for error, because restrictions on one topic suppress connected ideas elsewhere.
If an institution becomes hostile to inquiry, create a smaller space with explicit norms for independent work instead of expecting a conventional majority to change quickly.

title: Modeling a Wealth Tax
exclusion_reason: A compounding calculation of hypothetical wealth-tax effects on founder stock; it addresses tax policy and personal holdings, not company formation, funding mechanics, product, users, team, or operating decisions.

title: Early Work
candidate_workflows: When reviewing an ambitious early project, do not judge it as finished work; switch from listing reasons it cannot work to finding paths by which it could, and weight predictions by outcome rather than hit rate.
Preserve demanding taste while temporarily lowering the standard applied to the first version; track rate of improvement so an ugly but rapidly improving project is not killed prematurely.
Use a fast, low-commitment medium and label the first attempt a sketch, hack, or experiment; define what the test can rule out and vary the approach when failure leaves a plausible path.
Seek peers working on comparably difficult new projects who can distinguish an ugly duckling from weak work, rather than surrounding the project with indiscriminate encouragement.
Study accurate histories and first versions of successful work to recalibrate how little promise an ambitious project may show at the start.

title: How to Think for Yourself
candidate_workflows: For work where novelty is essential, including startup ideas, seek a proposition that sounds wrong to most people but that domain evidence makes correct; do not confuse consensus approval with validation.
Maintain a small set of independent-minded peers and participate in multiple intellectually different groups so local consensus has less control and useful ideas can cross domains.
Treat accepted claims as puzzles: ask whether each is true, label degrees of belief instead of collapsing uncertainty to certainty or impossibility, and follow curiosity toward neglected questions.

As a startup grows, audit whether hiring and communication systems are diluting independent thought; hire for independent judgment, protect small subteams, and consider automation or outsourcing for work whose staffing would damage the culture.
When possible, grow revenue without proportional headcount so organizational scale does not automatically replace the early team's independent operating style.

title: The Airbnbs
candidate_workflows: Evaluate a founding team through observable execution: whether they take notes, implement advice before the next check-in, generate follow-on ideas, and sustain unusually high effort.

When growth is absent but founders have first-hand evidence of a valuable new behavior, define one final bounded attempt and a concrete ramen-profitability threshold instead of persisting or quitting vaguely.
Use demand data to identify the hottest initial market, go there in person, help users improve the supply manually, and record what their urgent circumstances reveal about the product's mission.
Track weekly revenue or usage closely enough to distinguish noise from a real change in slope, and keep accelerating once the initial market becomes self-sustaining.

title: Billionaires Build
candidate_workflows: Map a path from a small existing market to a large future one, but require a real seed group who urgently wants the imperfect product now; identify those first users and the evidence of their demand.

Develop founder-market expertise through first-hand use, prototypes, and direct conversations until the founders can teach an investor what users need and answer detailed questions without relying on a polished pitch.

In an investor interview, answer the question asked, admit unknowns and explain how to resolve them, and describe failure modes, competitors, strengths, and weaknesses in expert detail instead of presenting a perfect facade.
Assess the team's ability to find the market through domain knowledge, building ability, resilience, cofounder trust, and concrete stories of resourceful collaboration under constraint.
Test whether genuine interest in the problem will sustain the founders after status or money stops motivating them, and keep delighting users as the operating lodestar at every scale.

title: Earnestness
candidate_workflows: Assess founder motivation on both direction and magnitude: look for genuine interest in the problem plus sustained effort, and combine that earnestness with evidence of capability rather than treating sincerity alone as sufficient.

Use behavior under hard problems to distinguish intrinsic interest from status or money seeking; people who care about the work itself are more likely to persist when shortcuts and early exits appear.
When choosing a field or venture, ask whether deep care improves outcomes and whether technical curiosity can align with economic value; avoid domains where performative cynicism is rewarded instead.
Allow bounded naive optimism to reopen problems whose established assumptions may have decayed, while continuing to test the founder's knowledge and execution.

title: What I Worked On
candidate_workflows: Test whether an entry-level product can improve upward until it compresses a high-end incumbent against the ceiling; treat high-end prestige as a danger signal rather than proof of defensibility.

When an initial customer hypothesis fails, inspect what the current technology already does for an adjacent market and build the smallest prototype that proves the new delivery model before committing to the full company.
Serve the first users manually even when doing so seems to contradict the product's premise; use the work to learn the domain and the product experience, then build what repeats.
Judge a startup by growth rate as well as absolute size, and keep hiring below the point where burn makes the company need investors despite strong growth.

When designing a founder service or institution, start from pains the builders experienced directly, prototype a simple structure, and use cohorts and alumni networks to reduce isolation, share support, and create initial customer relationships.

Audit attention by asking whether the largest recurring stressor is central to the mission; remove noncore obligations that dominate operations, and prepare succession before the organization consumes every other valuable project.
Treat low prestige and obsolete custom as discovery signals in fast-changing fields, while still validating the underlying work rather than choosing marginality for its own sake.

title: Donate Unrestricted
exclusion_reason: Advice to donors about unrestricted nonprofit gifts and asymmetric donor relationships; it provides no startup or company workflow despite a possible generic analogy to delegation and trust.

title: Write Simply
candidate_workflows: Write product, investor, and team communication with ordinary words and simple sentences so readers spend attention on the idea rather than decoding the prose.
Review difficult material for non-native readers and remove complexity that is not required by the subject; use unusual words or sentence structures only when their effect is deliberate.
Use simple language as an honesty test: if a claim has little substance, clarity should expose that before it reaches the audience.
Draft quickly, then edit over multiple passes with an emphasis on cutting until every remaining complication earns its place.

title: How People Get Rich Now
candidate_workflows: When interpreting company-formation data, separate ordinary new businesses from startups designed for rapid scale so aggregate trends do not mislead the decision.
Look for technology that lowers product-building or customer-acquisition costs enough to let a new entrant punch through an incumbent market rather than competing only in a predefined tech category.

Preserve founder leverage by keeping the initial capital requirement low; raise additional money by choice to accelerate a working company, not because a high fixed cost makes investor permission necessary for survival.

Model founder equity value as a function of both revenue and growth rate: faster growth reaches scale sooner and makes the same revenue stream more valuable, but larger rounds help only if they improve success or extend runway.

title: The Real Reason to End the Death Penalty
exclusion_reason: A legal and political argument against capital punishment based on wrongful convictions and case examples; it contains no reusable startup, maker, team, product, user, work, or communication workflow.

title: An NFT That Saves Lives
exclusion_reason: A promotional description of one nonprofit NFT fundraiser and its impact arithmetic; it offers no reusable startup product, customer, team, operating, or fundraising workflow.

title: Crazy New Ideas
candidate_workflows: Gate an implausible idea first on the proposer's reasonableness and relevant domain expertise; when both are strong, treat the apparent craziness as possible evidence of a hidden insight rather than automatic incompetence.

Replace an immediate verdict with questions that locate the disagreement between the expert's model and yours; determine what either side would need to learn and judge the bet by expected value, not probability of success alone.
Before dismissing a new idea, inspect whether envy, status, allegiance, vested interests, or the current paradigm are driving the reaction rather than evidence.
Study how important ideas looked in their unfinished early form, and give credible innovators enough encouragement and inquiry to develop the idea without pretending success is guaranteed.

title: Fierce Nerds
candidate_workflows: When evaluating a technical founder or leader, do not mistake social diffidence for lack of drive; assess competitiveness, independent judgment, problem-solving impatience, and demonstrated work rather than conversational polish.
Channel overconfidence, competitiveness, and impatience into an ambitious hard project where progress provides feedback and prevents unused drive from turning into cynical attack.

Place highly driven technical people in small groups where getting the right answer matters more than preserving superficial harmony, while explicitly requiring them to control interruption and other needlessly abrasive behavior.

Treat recurring bitterness or reflexive idea-shooting as a warning that ambition is not attached to constructive work, and redirect the person toward a difficult owned problem before it hardens into team damage.
